summary: Discovery call with Aurora to scope migration from OpenAI hosted to Redwood Dedicated. Main concerns: eval parity, tokenization/embedding differences, latency/cost tradeoffs, VPC/KMS requirements, and pilot benchmarks. Agreed next steps: send pricing/SOW, share benchmark template, schedule benchmark run.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Kim (Redwood SE), Maya Rivera (CTO, Aurora), Leo Zhang (Head of ML), Priya Nair (Platform Engineer)

Auto-generated summary: (may be imperfect)
- Aurora evaluating migration from OpenAI (hosted) to a Dedicated Redwood deployment for cost and data control.
- Primary evals: inference parity, latency/cost, compatibility with existing vLLM/TGI-based stack, and security controls (VPC/KMS/SOC2).

00:00 - Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we really appreciate you taking the time, i'm Samir AE on the Redwood side, with Jules our SE. quick agenda, hear your current setup, major pain points, then we can talk about dedicated and next steps.
00:18 - Maya: Thanks Samir, yeah appreciate it. Quick background: Aurora's building a patient-facing summarization product and a clinical QA assistant. Right now we're on OpenAI hosted for generation and embeddings, but costs are ballooning and we need tighter data controls.
00:34 - Leo: yeah also we have a bunch of infra we want to reuse, we run vLLM for internal experiments and some TGI endpoints for lower-cost inference. main ask is we need a path to move without major accuracy regressions.
00:50 - Jules: got it. when you say accuracy regressions — are you talking instruction-following outputs or embedding similarity changes?
01:02 - Leo: both. embeddings drift is the big thing for search relevancy. We saw small differences between OpenAI and our local vLLM quantized runs — nearest neighbor sets shuffle a bit.
01:20 - Priya: And from platform side, we need VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs shipped to Splunk. SOC2 is in scope.
01:32 - Samir: totally makes sense. quick question on timeline — are you looking to pilot in the next month? quarter?
01:40 - Maya: Ideally a POC in 3-4 weeks, production in 2-3 months if the numbers look good.
01:46 - Samir: ok good. jj.. jules, want to run through how Redwood Dedicated can map to their constraints?
01:55 - Jules: sure. so Dedicated gives you a tenant backed by reserved GPU capacity. you get the same API surface as hosted — generation, chat, embeddings, streaming — but you can deploy in a VPC and bring your own KMS. we also support private control plane options for enterprise.
02:15 - Maya: Are the models the same as hosted? like, will evals be identical to OpenAI responses?
02:24 - Jules: Good question. Redwood hosts a catalog of open models and verified performance profiles. If you're comparing to OpenAI proprietary models, exact parity isn't guaranteed. For open-weight models you can get near-identical behavior if you use the same checkpoints and tokenizer. for hosted-to-dedicated parity — it's the same runtime, so you shouldn't see changes due to serving, — although quantization and kernel choices can affect outputs slightly.
02:48 - Leo: So we run GPT-like models in vLLM with 8-bit quantization and a custom tokenizer for some preproc, how does Redwood handle tokenization differences?
03:00 - Jules: Redwood's runtime uses the model's tokenizer by default and we expose tokenization options. For vLLM or TGI checkpoints we can load the same tokenizer and weights. The places where drift happen are usually ops-level quantization differences or fused-kernel numerics. For the pilot we recommend running side-by-side evals: your vLLM runs vs Redwood Dedicated with the same checkpoint and quantization profile.
03:25 - Priya: Are there any tools from Redwood to help automate those evals? we want to run 5k prompts overnight and compare embeddings + generations.
03:33 - Jules: Yep, we have a benchmark template and a comparison harness we can share. It computes ranking/recall deltas, embedding cosine differences, and generation n-gram overlap. We'll also help interpret where differences come from — kernel precision, batch sizes, etc.
03:50 - Samir: and on the infra side, we can do a realistic benchmark with identical sequence length distributions and traffic patterns to approximate your production tail latency.
04:02 - Maya: Cost question: OpenAI pricing is per token and our monthly bill is high for heavy summarization. What does Dedicated look like?
04:10 - Samir: Dedicated is reserved capacity — you commit to a cluster size monthly. Unit cost per token is much lower at scale but you pay for reservation. We can run a cost projection for your traffic shape.
04:23 - Leo: will we be able to burst to hosted if dedicated is saturated?
04:30 - Jules: Yes, hybrid routing is supported. policy-based routing can fallback to hosted or cheaper model variants. That said, for data-residency sensitive requests we'd keep them on Dedicated per policy.
04:45 - Priya: Security — SSO, SAML, RBAC? we need integration with Okta and fine-grained roles.
04:53 - Samir: we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. For Dedicated/Private deployments you can also enforce network restrictions and KMS integration. We'll include SOC2 docs and our private deployment checklist.
05:10 - Maya: On the model side, we have some inference-specific tooling: batching, KV cache sharing across pods. Does Redwood runtime support KV cache reuse so chat sessions don't re-run context?
05:22 - Jules: Yes — the runtime has KV cache management and continuous batching. For multi-turn history we keep KV cache local to the session and we have strategies to shard across GPUs. There are also options for cache warm start for high-QPS sessions.
05:40 - Leo: any gotchas with our current TGI deployments? we use TGI for lower-cost CPU inference on long tail queries. we want to keep that layer.
05:50 - Jules: TGI checkpoints can be exported and run on Redwood if they match supported architectures. CPU-based TGI runs are fine for low-throughput, but Dedicated is focused on GPU-backed serving. You could keep TGI for cheap fallback.
06:05 - Maya: How quickly can you spin up a Dedicated cluster for a pilot?
06:12 - Samir: For a pilot we can provision a small reserved pool in ~2 weeks once contractual terms and infra details like VPC peering are confirmed. Private on-prem is longer.
06:23 - Priya: Talking about metrics: we care about p95 latency, tail latency, token/sec throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. we may want to set SLOs.
06:34 - Jules: we can surface per-route p95 and token-level cost in the Redwood Console. Also tracing hooks and per-model dashboards for regressions.
06:45 - Leo: we ran into an issue before where embeddings from different infra versions gave different dimensional scaling due to normalization differences. can you guarantee embedding vector shape and normalization?
06:58 - Jules: vector dimensionality is determined by the model weights. normalization defaults should match the model's reference implementation; however, we can expose post-processing hooks to ensure your pipeline applies the same L2 normalization. We'll make sure normalization is identical in the benchmark harness.
07:15 - Maya: Regulatory — data residency for EU patients. we need region control, can you run Dedicated in eu-west-1?
07:23 - Samir: yes, we have Dedicated in NA and EU regions, and Private deployments can be hosted in your region as well. we'll flag that in the SOW.
07:32 - Priya: One operational question: how do model rollouts look? we need canary and rollback and the ability to pin model versions per route.
07:41 - Jules: Rollouts supported — canary, A/B, automatic fallback. you can pin versions per route and define traffic splits; Console shows quality metrics per rollout.
07:55 - Maya: For the POC we'll need sample security docs and a cost estimate to present to our procurement.
08:02 - Samir: we'll send the SOC2 + security pack and a conservative cost projection.
08:08 - Leo: Regarding compatibility — is Redwood API a drop-in for OpenAI's API?
08:14 - Jules: Redwood's API is designed to be developer-friendly but it's not a verbatim OpenAI proxy. We support similar generation and embedding endpoints, streaming, and function calling patterns. For most apps it's a simple adapter layer; in complex systems you might need small changes for tokenization or model parameters. We can provide an adapter shim for the pilot.
08:36 - Priya: Any known differences when using function calling or structured outputs?
08:42 - Jules: Function calling semantics are supported but implementational details can differ; we'll validate structured output shapes during the evals.
08:50 - Maya: Can we try a quick demo of a single prompt run to see latency?
08:55 - Samir: we can do a lightweight hosted run now, but since you're comparing to Dedicated we should run the benchmark side-by-side. if you want i can do a quick hosted generation for the sample prompt.
09:08 - Maya: sure, here's one: "Summarize this patient progress note in two bullet points focusing on action items"
09:18 - Samir: (typing) ok sending…
09:30 - Samir: hosted response returned in 420ms. generation looks comparable to your prior results.
09:38 - Leo: sounds reasonable. we'll need measurements over longer contexts; summarization often hits 1.5k-3k tokens.
09:48 - Jules: for long sequences we optimize kernels and recommend longer KV cache-aware configs. we'll include guidance in the checklist.
10:00 - Priya: On the PII side, do you offer redaction or DLP integrations?
10:06 - Samir: Redwood doesn't do automated content redaction by default; that lives in the application layer. We can integrate DLP tools via hooks and before data lands in logs we can mask. For Dedicated we can disable logging for specific endpoints.
10:20 - Maya: Good. another question — how do you handle model updates? if you pin to a checkpoint, but downstream we need minor tuning, what's the process?
10:30 - Jules: you can pin a model version. If you need a tuned variant, we can host a custom variant or guide you to bring your fine-tuned weights. rollout then proceeds like any other model.
10:40 - Leo: Would you be open to letting us run vLLM in our infra and then have Redwood route to it? we want to avoid cold starts when you don't have capacity.
10:50 - Jules: We can support hybrid routing and even edge deployments in Private scenarios, but routing to customer-managed vLLM has operational complexity. For the pilot we recommend benchmarking on Redwood Dedicated first.
11:05 - Maya: Ok makes sense. What about the billing model for pilot — is there a trial credit or reduced reserved pricing?
11:12 - Samir: We typically offer a time-limited pilot pricing and can structure a smaller reserved pool for the pilot period. We'll include options in the SOW.
11:22 - Priya: Logistics: we'll need VPC peering info, subnets, and an SSH jump host for troubleshooting during POC.
11:30 - Samir: noted — Jules will send the infra checklist.
11:34 - Jules: i'll put together an infra checklist with VPC CIDRs, route table needs, KMS ARNs, and Splunk endpoint details.
11:44 - Leo: On evaluation metrics, we want per-prompt difference file and aggregated metrics like recall@k for embeddings. can you produce that as part of the benchmark deliverable?
11:55 - Jules: yes, deliverable includes per-prompt diffs, embedding cosine distributions, and a short findings doc pointing to likely causes.
12:06 - Maya: Will logs include prompt text? if so we need masking options.
12:12 - Samir: we can toggle logging and provide redaction guidance. Dedicated can be configured to not persist prompt text in logs.
12:24 - Priya: One more question on SLA: what uptime guarantees do you offer for Dedicated?
12:30 - Samir: Dedicated comes with an SLA; we'll include the exact uptime/credits language in the SOW.
12:36 - Maya: Great. Any last technical risks from your side we should be aware of?
12:41 - Jules: mostly the usual: evaluation mismatch due to quantization and tokenizer differences, and operational runbooks for VPC/KMS peering. We'll surface mitigation in the benchmark.
12:55 - Maya: ok let's recap next steps.
13:00 - Samir: recap: we'll send pricing + SOW, SOC2/security pack, infra checklist, and the benchmark template. Jules will help run the benchmark. Leo will provide prompt set (~5k) by 2025-11-20. Then we schedule a 2-hour benchmark run week of 2025-11-24. Does that capture it?
13:22 - Maya: yes.
13:24 - Priya: yes.
13:25 - Leo: yes.
13:27 - Samir: Perfect. we'll follow up via email and i'll drop calendar invites for the benchmark slot. thanks all.
13:34 - Maya: Thanks Samir, Jules.
13:37 - Jules: thanks everyone, talk soon.
13:40 - End of recording.

Notes: transcript contains typical ASR artifacts; speaker attribution approximate. References to vLLM/TGI/OpenAI may be spelled inconsistently in auto-transcript. Links shared: Pricing_Sheet_v1 (link), SOC2_Audit_Summary.pdf (link), Benchmark_Template.csv (link).
